chunks: Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sufi, saying: He narrated to us Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Isma'il, saying: I heard Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas saying:

When Al-Ma'mun pledged allegiance to Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him), the Imam (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful! Sincerity is obligatory for you, and deceit is not fitting for a believer. The masses dislike what you did to me, and the elites dislike what you did to Al-Fadl ibn Sahl. The opinion is for you to distance us from yourself until your affairs are rectified.' Ibrahim said: 'By God, these were his words, the cause of what the matter ended up in.'

key_terms.الْفَضْلِ بْنِ سَهْلٍ: Al-Fadl ibn Sahl, a powerful vizier

ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam Ar-Ridha give to Al-Ma'mun regarding their political relationship?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (a.s.) advised Caliph al-Ma'mun to distance the Ahl al-Bayt from the political center to mitigate the dissatisfaction of both the general public and the elite regarding the recent appointment of Fadl ibn Sahl. This strategic withdrawal, intended to preserve the Imam's spiritual integrity and political safety, ultimately set the stage for his martyrdom, as noted by Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas. The narrative highlights the delicate balance between political acceptance and spiritual independence in Shia history.
